icons.label: 重击
icons.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONE square martial-ability icon as part of the SAME FAMILY as the supplied uppercut sample. Input image 1 is the edit target and the canonical CHARACTER, FRAME, PALETTE, FINISH and LIGHTING reference.
Preserve the reference rounded-square silver frame: identical canvas placement, thickness on all four sides, corner radius and restrained bevel. Preserve transparent pixels outside the frame. Preserve the near-black charcoal interior. Change only the pose of the character, the position of the same sword, and the action trail.
Character identity lock: the exact same neutral faceless athletic figure, smooth featureless head, same head-to-body ratio and limb proportions, same plain dark fitted long-sleeved training tunic, trousers, simple boots and minimal wrist bands as the reference. NO new helmet, face, hair, armor, cloak, skirt, insignia or ornaments. Keep the same cool dark-gray figure, soft broad shading and restrained silver rim light. One character only, two arms, two legs, two hands gripping one single longsword. No duplicate motion-copy characters.
Style lock: premium restrained hand-painted action-RPG ability illustration with clean contours, broad smooth shading, dark body subordinate to bright ivory-silver sword and slash. Not a chunky embossed badge, metal statue, cartoon, line drawing or full environment. Readable at 48px. Entire figure, feet, sword and action effect comfortably inside the rounded frame. No text, labels, numbers, watermarks, UI panels or scenery.
The action must be immediately distinct from the reference upward slash.
ACTION: HEAVY STRIKE. Show the figure completing a powerful TWO-HANDED OVERHEAD DOWNWARD CHOP. A compact planted wide stance with both boots grounded, bent knees and torso folding slightly forward into the blow. Both hands hold the hilt in front of the body; the long sword angles sharply DOWN toward the lower-left interior. A single thick clean almost-vertical crescent trail falls from above the figure's head down to the lowered blade, clearly expressing accumulated weight and downward force. A small sharp silver contact flash at the low end supports the impact; do not add rubble, rocks, cracks or debris. Keep the figure large and the short heavy downward arc bold, not a running lunge, thrust or uppercut.
